veranderings.na: Die mense onder Shaka se beheer
veranderings.rede: The block opens with a pronoun whose referent is only in the previous block; naming Shaka makes the block clear on its own.

veranderings.voor: Dit het ook op beeste, eerbetoon en die handel gerus.
veranderings.na: Dit het ook op beeste, eerbetoon en die handel berus.
veranderings.rede: The previous sentence says 'berus'; using the same verb in the paired sentence reads more smoothly and avoids a needless switch.

veranderings.voor: Hulle weerspreek mekaar soms en oordryf dinge.
veranderings.na: Hulle het mekaar soms weerspreek en dinge oordryf.
veranderings.rede: The traders are historical people described in the past tense in the surrounding sentences; the past tense keeps the tense consistent.

vlae.teks: Lank voor Shaka het 'n vroeë opperhoof mag gehad as mense hom wou volg.
vlae.rede: 'as' can be read as 'when' or 'if', and the sentence does not make clear that the point is that the chief's power depended on people choosing to follow him; clarifying it (e.g. with 'net' or 'solank') would add a qualifier, so the writer should decide the intended meaning.
